title: Cylinder 2 Contribution/Balance Fault (Low)
shortDescription: The PCM detected an imbalance in cylinder 2 contribution, biased low, indicating an injector or fueling fault.
fullDescription: DTC P0270 sets when the powertrain control module determines that cylinder 2 is contributing less torque than expected relative to the other cylinders. This typically points to an injector flow issue, electrical fault, or mechanical compression problem on that cylinder.
safetyImpact: Cylinder misfires can cause loss of power and may damage the catalytic converter over time.

causes.cause: Low fuel pressure or clogged injector

symptoms: Misfire or rough running on cylinder 2

fixSteps.title: Scan and Verify Code
fixSteps.instruction: Use an OBD-II scanner to confirm the active code and capture freeze-frame data for the affected cylinder.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Injector Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the injector connector for the affected cylinder. Inspect for chafed wires, corrosion, or loose pins. Wiggle test while monitoring data.

fixSteps.title: Test Injector Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure injector coil resistance with a multimeter and compare against spec (typically 10-16 ohms for high-impedance).

fixSteps.title: Replace Injector or Repair Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: If injector is out of spec, replace it. If wiring is damaged, repair the harness and clear the code, then road test.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive with a P027x code for cylinder 2?
faq.a: Brief drives are usually fine, but a misfiring injector can damage the catalytic converter and worsen fuel economy. Repair promptly.

faq.q: What does 'contribution/balance' mean?
faq.a: The PCM compares each cylinder's contribution to engine torque. If one cylinder is too low or too high, this code sets.

faq.q: Can I just clean the injector?
faq.a: Sometimes ultrasonic cleaning restores function, but if the coil is electrically out of spec, replacement is required.

fullDescription: DTC P0286 sets when the powertrain control module determines that cylinder 10 is contributing less torque than expected relative to the other cylinders. This typically points to an injector flow issue, electrical fault, or mechanical compression problem on that cylinder.
safetyImpact: Cylinder misfires can cause loss of power and may damage the catalytic converter over time.

causes.cause: Low fuel pressure or clogged injector

symptoms: Misfire or rough running on cylinder 10

fixSteps.title: Scan and Verify Code
fixSteps.instruction: Use an OBD-II scanner to confirm the active code and capture freeze-frame data for the affected cylinder.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Injector Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Locate the injector connector for the affected cylinder. Inspect for chafed wires, corrosion, or loose pins. Wiggle test while monitoring data.

fixSteps.title: Test Injector Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure injector coil resistance with a multimeter and compare against spec (typically 10-16 ohms for high-impedance).

fixSteps.title: Replace Injector or Repair Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: If injector is out of spec, replace it. If wiring is damaged, repair the harness and clear the code, then road test.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive with a P027x code for cylinder 10?
faq.a: Brief drives are usually fine, but a misfiring injector can damage the catalytic converter and worsen fuel economy. Repair promptly.

faq.q: What does 'contribution/balance' mean?
faq.a: The PCM compares each cylinder's contribution to engine torque. If one cylinder is too low or too high, this code sets.

faq.q: Can I just clean the injector?
faq.a: Sometimes ultrasonic cleaning restores function, but if the coil is electrically out of spec, replacement is required.
